record.original_question: Are there transcendental entire functions f such that every Liouville number x is sent to another Liouville number f(x)?

evidence.quote: Question 3.27 (Mahler). Are there entire transcendental functions f (z) such that if x is a Liouville number then so is f (x)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A real number x is called a Liouville number if x is irrational and for every positive integer n there exist integers p and q with q > 1 such that
    0 < |x - p/q| < 1/q^n.
An entire function f : C → C is called transcendental if it is not a polynomial (equivalently, f is not algebraic over C(z)).

Does there exist a transcendental entire function f : C → C such that f(x) is a Liouville number for every Liouville number x ∈ R?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, originally posed by Mahler in 1984, remains open in full generality. Partial results are known: Marques and Moreira constructed transcendental entire functions mapping an uncountable subset of Liouville numbers (the "ultra-Liouville" numbers) into the Liouville numbers, but the existence of a transcendental entire function sending every Liouville number to a Liouville number has not been established.

status_evidence.title: On a question proposed by K. Mahler concerning Liouville numbers
status_evidence.snippet: Marques and Moreira prove the existence of an uncountable subset of Liouville numbers and uncountably many transcendental entire functions mapping this set into the Liouville numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial progress is known; the full Mahler question remains open.

status_evidence.title: On a variant of a question proposed by K. Mahler concerning Liouville numbers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a variant of Mahler's question, indicating the original question is still considered open.
status_evidence.claim: Mahler's original question on Liouville numbers continues to be studied as an open problem.
